allowed_dependency_manifest.content: Let n, k, l ∈ Z with 0 ≤ k, l ≤ n. Define R(q) = [n choose k]_q / [n choose l]_q in the natural rational-function setting for Gaussian q-binomial coefficients. If R(q) lies in a polynomial ring in q (i.e., R(q) has only finitely many nonnegative powers of q with coefficients in the relevant coefficient ring), then when written as R(q) = Σ_i c_i q^i, every coefficient c_i satisfies c_i ≥ 0.

forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, l with 0 ≤ k, l ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose l]_q is a polynomial in q, then that polynomial has only nonnegative coefficients.

forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260324204708_474b5c77
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: For integers A, B, d with A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0, define Q_{A,B,d}(q) := prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(A+i)) / (1 - q^(B+i)), with the empty product equal to 1 when d = 0. Assume Q_{A,B,d}(q) belongs to Q[q]. Let S be the weighted polynomial ring Q[x_1, ..., x_d] graded by deg(x_i) = B+i; when d = 0 interpret S as Q. Then there exist homogeneous polynomials f_1, ..., f_d in S such that deg(f_i) = A+i for every i, and for each i the image of f_i in S/(f_1, ..., f_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor. Equivalently, Q_{A,B,d}(q) is realized by a homogeneous regular sequence in a weighted polynomial ring with variable weights B+1, ..., B+d and relation degrees A+1, ..., A+d.

semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all integers A,B,d with A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0, define w_j = B + j for j = 1,...,d and E = {A + 1,...,A + d}. Assume that for every positive integer n, the number of indices j in {1,...,d} with n dividing w_j is at most the number of elements e in E with n dividing e. Then for every nonempty subset J of {1,...,d}, the cardinality of the intersection of E with Sigma(J) is at least the cardinality of J.

witness_dependencies: To state membership of an element e in Sigma(J), there must exist a choice of nonnegative integers m_j (one for each j in J) such that e equals the sum over j in J of m_j times w_j; these coefficients depend on J and on the chosen e.
For the conclusion, for each nonempty J there are at least |J| distinct elements e in E such that e is in Sigma(J); the particular elements e and their representing coefficients depend on J.

payload.statement_nl: Let A,B,d be integers with A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0. For j=1,...,d put w_j := B+j and let E := {A+1,...,A+d}. Assume that for every positive integer n one has #{ j in {1,...,d} : n divides w_j } <= #{ e in E : n divides e }. For each subset J of {1,...,d}, define Sigma(J) := { sum_{j in J} m_j w_j : each m_j is a nonnegative integer }. Then for every nonempty subset J of {1,...,d}, at least |J| elements of E lie in Sigma(J); equivalently, #(E intersect Sigma(J)) >= |J|.

suspected_gaps: I could not resolve the main gcd-1 case. A natural reduction divides by g = gcd{w_j : j in J} and passes to the consecutive block of multiples of g in the two intervals, but this only reduces the problem when g>1. For gcd(J)=1, I did not find a rigorous argument from the given divisibility-count hypothesis to force at least |J| elements of E into the numerical semigroup Σ(J).

Several promising approaches break down: pure divisibility matching is too weak; generic conductor/Frobenius bounds are not sharp enough; and an induction on proper subsets of J leaves an unresolved union-size problem in the minimal gcd-1 case.

result_payload.stuck_point: The unresolved point is this: for a nonempty subset J with gcd(w_j : j in J)=1, I could not prove from the hypothesis #{w in {B+1,...,B+d} : n|w} <= #{e in E : n|e} for all n that the interval E={A+1,...,A+d} must contain at least |J| values representable by the semigroup generated by J. I can reduce the general case g>1 to a smaller interval problem by dividing by g and looking only at multiples of g, but that does not handle the terminal gcd-1 case.
